A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CFM research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original concept-quality measurements, a human study, classification, captioning, segmentation, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original human-study and downstream-task results, together with architecture ablations, backbone-scaling experiments, hierarchy-direction evaluation, and quantitative caption steering.

M1.justification: The core CFM pipeline is retained, but the stated naming procedure changes in Eq. (B.8): alpha now scales the combined child and parent vectors, whereas v2 applied it only to the child vector. The accompanying explanation changes accordingly. This establishes a limited procedural revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, and underlying classification, segmentation, concept-assessment, and caption-steering tasks are retained. SigLIP-2 changes the model configuration; the systematic COCO steering and hierarchy-direction evaluations add protocols and analyses within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure C15 introduces a CLIP target-word steering baseline against CFM's concept steering; v2 supplied qualitative steering examples without this comparison. The comparator sets in the retained main classification, concept-quality, captioning, and segmentation experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include judging 1,000 hierarchy pairs using top-five examples and consistency/directionality filtering, and testing caption deletion with 80 samples per COCO category using text matching and an LLM judge. Appendix B.8 adds a 400M-parameter SigLIP-2 configuration and controlled ImageNet-trained architecture variants. These are added experimental settings, not demonstrated reruns of the retained headline experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's dictionary-size and reconstruction/sparsity analyses, v3 tests guided-pooling removal, alternative SAE objectives, sparsity effects on downstream performance and interpretability, and backbone scaling. It also adds hierarchy-direction validation and quantitative category-wise steering analysis. Table 2 extends the existing dictionary-size analysis with C2 scores.

E5.justification: The new relationship-judge prompt requests a confidence rating from 1 to 5, and Figure A6 displays an example rating. This adds limited per-judgment confidence reporting, rather than statistical uncertainty for aggregate accuracy. The existing Wilcoxon test is retained; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes CFM's C2 score from 0.405 to 0.465, and Figure C9 changes the plotted distributions. New results include 86.2% ImageNet accuracy for CFM with SigLIP-2, hierarchy-direction accuracy of 300/376 filtered pairs, and steering deletion rates of 25.9% versus 21.3% by LLM judging and 28.2% versus 23.2% by text matching. The per-dataset 4k/16k segmentation results from v2 Table B1 are omitted when condensed into v3 Table 2.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes the numerator's activation weight from A_ip to A_jp, making it consistent with the stated conditional-probability definition. Equations (3) and (4) replace argmin with argmax, matching the maximum-similarity rule; Eq. (3) also removes the bias from the prior-method expression. These are substantive mathematical corrections, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spatially grounded hierarchical concepts, improved naming, and interpretable foundation-model applications beyond classification with competitive downstream performance. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The added analyses explain guided pooling's importance, sparsity/locality/consistency tradeoffs, and applicability to a larger backbone. Figure C7 adds specific naming-failure interpretations, including lexical gaps and spurious correlations. Section C.8 qualifies steering effectiveness through category-dependent failures. The main conclusion and existing limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the relationship judge's full prompt, composite-image construction and filtering details, identifies the SigLIP-2 variant, and explicitly documents ImageNet-only SAE training for Appendix B.8. It also adds an interactive-visualization address. Existing core training hyperparameters and captioning hardware/time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The same 86 reference entries and substantive research positioning are retained. Corrections to existing CLIP-DINOiser and COCO-Object citations do not introduce new cited works or redefine the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3, expands B.8 and C.8, and makes localized grammar, terminology, caption, and cross-reference corrections. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands substantially: v2 Tables B1/B2 are condensed into main-text Table 2, new backbone and architecture tables are added, and new figures present the relationship-judge prompt/example and quantitative steering. Figure C9 is enlarged and redrawn with mean markers. Existing qualitative examples are retained, including the steering figure renumbered C16.

improvement.justification: v3 materially strengthens validation of the central design and steering claims. Controlled architecture ablations address questions left open by v2's narrower analyses, and quantitative steering supplies a baseline comparison beyond selected examples. Mathematical corrections also improve internal consistency. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed dictionary-size segmentation scores and the new steering text's reversal of the solid/hatched legend mapping. The hierarchy-direction result remains conditional on 376 of 1,000 sampled pairs, limiting its generality.
